title: Quadratic stabilization of the Foulkes–Howe map
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that the canonical Hermite-Hadamard-Howe map Sym^b(Sym^a V) -> Sym^a(Sym^b V) is surjective whenever a >= 2 and b >= a(a-1), for every finite-dimensional complex vector space V; the bound depends on a only and answers Landsberg's request for a polynomial bound. The course defines the map through symmetric tensors, describes its image by powers of products of vectors, and reduces surjectivity to the vanishing of symmetric multilinear forms on the diagonal at products; proves an injectivity lemma for directional derivatives with the Fischer inner product; and proves the vanishing by an induction that frees one slot with derivatives, applies the induction hypothesis, and removes a common power. A GL(V)-equivariant embedding Sym^a(Sym^b V) -> Sym^b(Sym^a V), as in Foulkes' conjecture, follows in the same range from the adjoint map.
prerequisites: linear algebra over the complex numbers: tensor products, quotient spaces, dual spaces, Hermitian inner products and adjoints
polynomials in several variables and their partial derivatives

checks.reading: The manuscript 'Quadratic stabilization of the canonical Foulkes-Howe map' (OpenAI, 25 Sep 2026; build/paper.tex and references.tex, 474 + 64 lines, 25 kB of TeX; local library copy openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 17 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written. No error was found. Changes of form in the course: (1) the diagonal criterion is stated with functionals on Sym^a(Sym^b V) and products in Sym(Sym^b V), without passing through invariant tensors; (2) the factorization of X^r + cY^r is justified by the product over roots of unity; (3) Corollary B (an equivariant embedding) is proved with the adjoint of the canonical map for GL(V)-compatible inner products, where the manuscript uses complete reducibility of polynomial representations (Macdonald), so the course needs no representation theory; (4) exercises add that products cannot be replaced by pure powers in the vanishing statement, and the surjectivity half of the sl2-type statement. Attributions checked: Landsberg, arXiv:1305.7387 (Section 7: Hermite, Hadamard, Howe, the Mueller-Neunhoeffer computation, Brion's bound; Problem 7.18 in the arXiv numbering, 7.19 in the published version); Raicu-Sam-Weyman, arXiv:2108.10910 (Section 2, Conjecture 2.10, the least stabilization degree open); Cheung-Ikenmeyer-Mkrtchyan, arXiv:1509.03944 (Theorem 6: kernels at (5,5) and (6,6), injectivity at (5,6)); Ikenmeyer arXiv:1509.04957 downloaded for McKay's propagation theorem, not cited in the lessons.

Ranks of the map, as the dimension of the span of P^a over random products P of b integer vectors, computed modulo the prime 2147483629 (a lower bound for the rank over Q): full rank in every tested case with b >= a(a-1): (a,b,dim V) = (2,2,2), (2,2,3), (2,2,4), (2,2,5), (2,3,3), (2,4,3), (3,6,2), (4,12,2) and (3,6,3) (rank 4060 of 4060, domain 5005); also (3,3,3) has full rank 220, and (3,2,3) is not surjective (domain 55 < codomain 56). The polarization identity for k <= 5; the Fischer inner product: adjointness on monomials, the commutator ED - DE = N_U - N_Y and the identity ||Dh||^2 - ||Eh||^2 = (p - q)||h||^2 on random bihomogeneous polynomials, exactly; a kernel element for p = q = 1; the factorization of X^r + cY^r for r <= 6; the derivative formulas D_(y,t) t^b = b t^(b-1) y and D_(x,v)^r v^b = (b!/(b-r)!) x^r v^(b-r) in Sym V.
